payload.statement_nl:
Let [m]_q = (1-q^m)/(1-q), let (a;q)_k = ∏_{j=0}^{k-1}(1-a q^j), let (a,b,c;q)_k = (a;q)_k (b;q)_k (c;q)_k, and let Φ_n(q) be the nth cyclotomic polynomial. Fix positive integers d and r with gcd(d,r)=1 and r <= d. Then there exists a nonnegative integer B such that for every integer n > 1 satisfying n ≡ 1 mod 2d there exists a Laurent polynomial in X over Z[q^±1] of the form C_{d,r,n}(X,q) = ∑_{j=-B}^{B} c_j(q) X^j, with each c_j(q) in Z[q^±1], having the following property. Define the modulus M_n(q) = [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2. For each integer k with 0 <= k <= n define
T_{d,r,n,k}(q) = [3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k^2 q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2} / (q^{2d};q^{2d})_k,
and define
G_{d,r,n,k}(q) = T_{d,r,n,k}(q) · C_{d,r,n}(q^k,q).
Also define
H_{d,r,n,0}(q) = [r]_q - [rn]_q q^{r(1-n)/2},
and for each integer k with 1 <= k <= n-1 define
H_{d,r,n,k}(q) = T_{d,r,n,k}(q).
Then H_{d,r,n,k}(q) = G_{d,r,n,k}(q) - G_{d,r,n,k+1}(q) for every integer k with 0 <= k <= n-1, and there exist polynomials A_0(q), B_0(q), A_n(q), and B_n(q) in Z[q] such that gcd(B_0(q), M_n(q)) = 1, gcd(B_n(q), M_n(q)) = 1, G_{d,r,n,0}(q) = M_n(q) A_0(q) / B_0(q), and G_{d,r,n,n}(q) = M_n(q) A_n(q) / B_n(q).

result_payload.candidate_counterexample: For any proposed uniform support bound B, set d=1, r=1, n=2B+13. Assume C(X,q)=∑_{j=-B}^B c_j(q)X^j satisfies the required telescoping identities for k=1,...,n-1. Writing X=q^k gives 1 = C(X,q) - R(X,q)C(qX,q) with R(X,q)=q^{-1}X^{-1}(1-q^4X^3)(1-qX^2)^3(1-qX)/((1-qX^3)(1+qX)). Clearing denominators yields a Laurent polynomial F(X,q) supported in X-exponents [-B,B+10]. Since F(q^k,q)=0 for 2B+12 values k=1,...,2B+12, Vandermonde implies F≡0. But the top X-degree term from -(1-q^4X^3)(1-qX^2)^3(1-qX)C(qX,q) is q^{m+8}c_m(q)X^{m+10} (where m is the top exponent of C), and this cannot be canceled by the other terms, whose X-degrees are at most m+5 and 5. Contradiction.

result_payload.reason: The submitted proof is empty, and the supplied counterexample family can be made rigorous. Fix d=r=1 and let B be any proposed uniform X-support bound. Take n=2B+13, which is admissible since n is odd. If C(X,q)=∑_{j=-B}^B c_j(q)X^j satisfied the telescoping identities for k=1,...,n-1, then with X=q^k those identities become 1 = C(X,q) - R(X,q) C(qX,q), where R(X,q)=q^{-1}X^{-1}(1-q^4X^3)(1-qX^2)^3(1-qX)/((1-qX^3)(1+qX)). After clearing denominators, F(X,q):=qX(1-qX^3)(1+qX)C(X,q) - (1-q^4X^3)(1-qX^2)^3(1-qX)C(qX,q) - qX(1-qX^3)(1+qX) is a Laurent polynomial in X with exponents contained in [-B,B+10], hence with at most 2B+11 X-monomials. But F(q^k,q)=0 for k=1,...,n-1=2B+12. Since the q^k are distinct over Q(q), the resulting Vandermonde system forces F(X,q)≡0. Now compare highest X-degree terms: if m is the largest exponent with c_m(q)≠0, then the second term contributes a nonzero X^{m+10} term q^{m+8}c_m(q)X^{m+10}, while the first term has X-degree at most m+5 and the final term has degree at most 5. So F cannot vanish identically. Contradiction. Therefore no such uniformly bounded-support certificate exists; the lemma statement is false.
